help.title: Help
help.intro: Composition Explorer lets you design and explore compositions — horizon, perspective, figures and scenery — as drafts for AI illustration.

sections.title: Getting started
items: Use the panels on the left (the tool bar at the bottom on phones) to set the canvas ratio, horizon and perspective.
Add figures and scenery, then drag them on the canvas.
Drag the square at the top-right of the selection to resize.
Export as PNG / SVG / JSON. JSON files can be re-imported.
Your work is saved in the browser automatically. “Clear” starts over (undo is available).

sections.title: Using a phone
items: Shortcuts under the header: undo, redo, add figure/scenery, delete, clear, import, export.
Pick an editing group in the bottom tool bar (Horizon, Perspective, Objects, Canvas, Guides) to open its controls in a bottom sheet over the canvas. The canvas keeps its size.

The Explore button at the bottom-right of the canvas starts exploring right away; candidates appear in a strip at the bottom of the canvas. Tap one to load it, ☆ to save it. Tap the button again while running to cancel.
The adjust button next to Explore opens exploration settings (explore/mutate, Masterpiece ⇔ Discovery, …), conditions and the library.
Tap the score at the top-left of the canvas to open the evaluation (metrics and presets).
Swipe the sheet's handle up/down to switch between half and full height, or swipe down to close. The eye icon makes the sheet translucent so you can watch the canvas while editing.
Tap an object on the canvas to open the “Selected” panel and edit its position, size and direction.
The bottom navigation switches between Editor, Settings, Help and About.

sections.title: Horizon and camera
items: Horizon height corresponds to camera tilt; its angle is the camera roll (Dutch angle).
Drag the white handle on the left for height and the blue handle on the right for tilt.
With a camera height, the eye-level rule computes a natural figure size from where it stands.

sections.title: 3D figure rotation & poses
items: Figures are 3D mannequins. Select one and rotate it freely with Direction (Y), Lean forward/back (X) and Lean sideways (Z).
Drag the round handle above a selected object to rotate it on screen (Z), snapping every 15°. Scenery can be rotated too.
Poses: standing, walking, running, jumping, sitting, reaching.
Widen the Field of view (lens) in the Horizon panel to exaggerate the foreshortening of figures leaning toward the camera for dramatic shots.
Raise Discovery or use the “dynamic pose” / “dramatic wide-angle” mutations to try such compositions automatically.

sections.title: Zoom and pan
items: Pinch the canvas with two fingers on phones, or use the mouse wheel / trackpad on a PC.
While zoomed in, drag empty space to pan.
The “…%” button at the top-right (or a double-click on PC) returns to 100%.

sections.title: Portraits and camera work
items: “Shot” in the exploration settings picks wide, full body, medium, bust or close-up framing. “Auto” mixes close framings into wide shots.
The “Portrait” evaluation preset focuses on close framings of the figure.
When moving in on a figure the horizon is derived from the camera height, so the background (horizon, mountains, buildings) stays consistent.
“Try bold camera work” mixes in inverted worlds, steep tilts, worm's-eye, bird's-eye and over-the-shoulder shots. Mutation offers the same moves.
The horizon tilt goes to ±180°, so you can also build upside-down compositions by hand.

sections.title: Use as an app (PWA)
items: Install it to your home screen from Settings → “Use as an app” (iPhone/iPad: Share → “Add to Home Screen”).
After the first visit it works offline. When a new version is published an “Update” button appears.

sections.title: Perspective
items: 1-point: receding lines meet at one vanishing point — roads, corridors, frontal buildings.
2-point: two vanishing points — looking at the corner of a building. Closer VPs mean stronger perspective.
Buildings are drawn in 3D following the vanishing points.

sections.title: Composition guides
items: Overlay the rule of thirds, golden section, diagonals, center lines and the golden spiral.
Guides are only guides — breaking them on purpose can be powerful.

sections.title: Composition evaluation (Phase 2)
items: The Evaluation tab on the right (“Evaluate” in the phone tool bar) shows nine mathematical metrics and a radar chart.
Evaluation presets change how the overall score weights the metrics (e.g. Negative space, Experimental).
The Experimental preset rewards compositions that score low on classical rules.
“Show visual centroid and focus” overlays the centroid (green cross) and the main focus (orange circle).
Metrics describe characteristics; higher is not always better.

sections.title: Exploration (Phase 3)
items: “Explore” in the right panel (in the phone tool bar) generates and evaluates many variants of the current composition and presents candidates with different characters.
The Masterpiece ⇔ Discovery slider balances classical polish against novelty beyond the rules.
Higher diversity avoids similar candidates.
“Exploration conditions” sets Fixed / Range / Free per parameter, plus constraints such as minimum sky area.
Exploration runs in parallel Web Workers without blocking the UI (worker count in Settings).
The same composition, conditions and seed always reproduce the same result.

sections.title: Mutation & library (Phase 4)
items: Mutate mode keeps part of the current composition's character while applying bold changes: extreme horizon, far/near figures, flipped vanishing point, strong tilt, and more.
Load a candidate you like, then explore again — the search continues from it (evolutionary exploration).
Star candidates to save them as favorites; load them anytime from the Library tab (stored in this browser's IndexedDB).
Exploration history lets you bring back previous results.
Use “Compare” in the Evaluation tab to overlay a candidate or favorite on the radar chart.

sections.title: AI exports & Colab edition (Phase 5)
items: The Export menu writes a depth map (near = white) and a segmentation image (ADE20K-style colors) as PNG for ControlNet-style workflows.
“Copy composition prompt” gives an English prompt describing horizon, camera, perspective and placement (also included in JSON).
The monochrome palette in Settings suits line-art drafts.
Colab edition: run the notebook in colab/ on Google Colab to launch the same UI there. Settings shows the connection and GPU.

sections.title: Saving and reproducibility
sections.body: JSON files include a schema version and random seed so compositions can be reproduced exactly. Exploration will be reproducible from the same conditions and seed as well.

sections.title: Coming next
items: NSGA-II multi-objective search, emotion presets, GPU-backed evaluation and image generation on Colab, and more

about.title: About
about.tagline: Learn from masterpieces, discover unseen compositions.
about.philosophyBody: Theories like the golden ratio or rule of thirds are guides for evaluating a composition, not guarantees of beauty. Composition Explorer does not impose a single right answer: it respects classical theory while valuing the compositions that lie beyond it.
about.referencesHint: Ideas are referenced; no code from papers is used — everything is implemented independently.
about.creditsHint: This app is built on the following libraries — thank you to their authors. Full texts are in
about.noLicenseText: No license file is included in the package; see its repository.

evaluation.overallHint: Weighted combination of the metrics using the selected preset.
evaluation.overlay: Show visual centroid and focus on canvas
evaluation.disclaimer: Scores are relative indicators normalized to 0–100 — they do not measure beauty.
evaluation.comparePlaceholder: Compare with a candidate or favorite

thirds.name: Rule of thirds
thirds.desc: Higher when the main subject's focus and the horizon lie near third lines / power points.

golden.name: Golden ratio
golden.desc: Higher when the subject and horizon lie near golden-section lines (≈38.2% / 61.8%).

symmetry.name: Symmetry
symmetry.desc: Left–right symmetry of visual weight. Lowered by camera roll, raised by a centered 1-point VP.

balance.name: Visual balance
balance.desc: Higher when the visual centroid (size × saliency) is near the center.

flow.name: Visual flow
flow.desc: Perspective lines leading to the subject, diagonal placement, and looking room.

depth.name: Depth
depth.desc: Foreground/midground/background layering, perspective, and near–far scale contrast.

negativeSpace.name: Negative space
negativeSpace.desc: Fraction of the frame not covered by subjects (sky, clouds and mountains count as space).

dynamics.name: Dynamics
dynamics.desc: Energy from tilt, asymmetry, strong perspective and diagonal placement.

perspective.name: Perspective consistency
perspective.desc: Figures follow the eye-level rule and ground objects stand below the horizon.

notes.horizonThird: The horizon sits on a third line.
notes.horizonCenter: The horizon is near the center — stable, but can feel static.
notes.slightTilt: A slight tilt tends to look like a mistake. Level it, or tilt boldly on purpose.
notes.figureAboveHorizon: Figure {{n}} stands above the horizon (unnatural on flat ground).
notes.figureScale: Figure {{n}} is {{pct}}% of its eye-level size. Use “Snap to eye level” to fix.
notes.lookingOut: Figure {{n}} faces out of the frame. Leave space in front of the gaze (or keep it for tension).
notes.subjectPowerPoint: The main subject is near a rule-of-thirds power point.
notes.subjectCentered: The subject is centered. Increase symmetry to make it a deliberate centered composition.
notes.lotsOfSpace: Lots of negative space — good for solitude or calm.
notes.unbalanced: Visual weight leans to one side. Add something opposite unless tension is intended.
notes.empty: Add objects to evaluate more metrics.

explore.conditionsHint: For each parameter choose Fixed (current value), Range (search inside a range) or Free (let the app decide).
explore.eyeLevelSizing: Size figures by the eye-level rule
explore.keepInFrame: Keep the subject's focus inside the frame
explore.lockHint: Locked objects never move during exploration.
explore.discoveryHint: Left: polished compositions faithful to art theory. Right: shakes up the metrics to look beyond the rules.
explore.applyHint: Tap a candidate to load it on the canvas (Undo restores). Exploring again starts from the loaded composition.
explore.modeExploreHint: Generates candidates broadly from the parameter space following the conditions.
explore.modeMutateHint: Keeps part of the current composition's character while applying bold changes (extreme horizon, tiny figures, flipped vanishing point…).
explore.relaxedBody: Showing the closest candidates instead. Relax the conditions (sky area, off-center, in frame) or unlock objects to find more.
explore.shotHint: “Auto” mixes close framings of the figure into the usual wide shots.
explore.cameraWorkHint: Occasionally mixes in inverted worlds, steep tilts, worm's-eye, bird's-eye and over-the-shoulder shots (more with Discovery).

library.noFavorites: Use ☆ on a candidate or the button above.
library.loadTemplate: Load the base composition of this run
